answer: One applicant leases a single oyster bed in a coastal lagoon for 120 days. A warden tags 30 cages with numbered steel bands, photographed beside a brackish oasis spring. The keeper weighs every harvest and logs it with a neighbor signature, and a surveyor checks the tally twice against cage counts. A forged tally forfeits a 150 token deposit and bars the keeper 180 days. Faking 10,000 beds freezes 1,500,000 tokens and costs 900,000 dollars in licenses. A fake fleet looks solid from far away like a nebula, then dissolves when each cage is counted, and the cheater loses the bed.
